angles: Fill in every field of the profile on the platforms buyers use (Zillow, Realtor.com, the brokerage page) with the website link and one identical name, phone and licence number.
Publish a quarterly local market note (median price, days on market, inventory for each city served) with one chart, and send it to the local news site and the chamber newsletter.
Build a preferred-vendor page of real partners (lender, title or escrow, inspector, stager, mover) and ask each to list the agent back on their resources page.
Sponsor a youth team, school fundraiser or neighbourhood event; ask for the sponsor-page link.
Apply to the editorial 'best agents' lists whose selection criteria you meet; skip the lists that charge to be included unless the client treats it as advertising.
Host a first-time-buyer or downsizing workshop and get it on the chamber, library and city event calendars.
Write city and neighbourhood guides worth quoting (schools, commute, parks); local sites and AI answers cite these.
avoid: Paying a 'Top 100 agents' site that sells rankings without labelling it advertising.
Buying links on real-estate blogs or 'Realtor SEO' networks.
Reviews written by the agent, paid for, or from people who were not clients; also breaks real-estate advertising rules.
Showing awards or ranks you cannot prove; the state's advertising rules apply (see the licence-number rule in rules/industries/real-estate-agent.json).
